title: 萨宾妇女走入战阵
summary: 罗马人在节庆中掳走萨宾妇女，随后与前来讨还女儿的亲族交战。被迫处于双方之间的妇女走入战阵阻止杀戮，促成共同统治，但和解并不能洗去掳掠的伤害。
paragraphs: 罗马建城传说中，新城缺少女子，向邻邦求婚又遭到拒绝。罗慕路斯便举行节庆，邀请周围居民携家人观看比赛，随后发出信号，让罗马男子抢走前来的年轻妇女。李维记述的这场掳掠不是自愿结亲；受害者被带离父母，所谓婚姻首先建立在强制与背叛宾客信任之上。
萨宾亲族没有接受既成事实，国王提图斯塔提乌斯带军攻打罗马。双方在城中激战时，被掳的妇女奔入兵刃之间，披散头发，恳求父亲与丈夫停止互相杀害。她们已经被迫与两个阵营发生联系，无论哪边获胜，失去父亲或丈夫的痛苦都将落在自己与孩子身上。
妇女的介入使战斗停下，两方首领随后议和，决定把居民合成一个共同体，由罗慕路斯和塔提乌斯共同统治。这是罗马作者解释早期共同体如何吸纳萨宾人的传统，不是可以独立核实的建城实录。妇女成功制止了眼前的杀戮，也不能反过来证明最初的掳掠正当或出于双方自愿。

en.title: The Sabine Women Enter the Battle
en.summary: Roman men abduct visiting women during a festival, provoking war with their Sabine relatives. The women intervene between the armies and help secure shared government. Their success in stopping further bloodshed does not excuse the coercion that created the conflict.
paragraphs: In Rome’s foundation tradition, the new settlement lacked women and failed to obtain marriage alliances with neighboring communities. Romulus invited families to a festival, then signaled his men to seize the young female visitors. Livy’s account describes an abduction, not a voluntary exchange of brides. The subsequent households began with coercion and the betrayal of people attending as guests.

The Sabines eventually marched under Titus Tatius to recover their relatives and attack Rome. During the fighting, the abducted women entered the space between the armies, their hair disordered, and appealed to fathers and husbands alike. Their forced position connected them to both sides. Whichever army won, the continuing slaughter would leave them mourning relatives and expose their children to further loss.

The intervention halted the battle and led the leaders to negotiate. Romans and Sabines formed a single community under the joint rule of Romulus and Tatius. Roman writers used this tradition to explain the incorporation of Sabines into early Rome; it is not an independently verified foundation record. Ending the immediate violence did not make the original seizure consensual or justified.

title: 努马与林泉中的埃革里亚
summary: 努马继位后希望约束罗马的战争习性，声称在林中向女神埃革里亚请教祭仪。传说把宗教制度归于这场相会，诗人又写他死后女神悲泣，最终化成泉水。
paragraphs: 罗慕路斯之后，罗马传说中的第二任国王努马被请来治理城市。面对惯于用兵的居民，他试图用祭仪、节期与神圣约束改变生活的节奏。李维记述他常独自进入有泉水的林地，并宣称在那里与埃革里亚相会，关于敬神的安排都是听从这位女神的教导而制定。
努马设立或整理祭司职务，把不同神明的祭礼交给相应人员，又划分历法，使人们知道何时举行公共仪式。林中会谈为这些安排赋予神圣权威，而不是留下可供旁人旁听的议事记录。李维的叙述也把这种说法放在国王治理人心的策略中，不能直接当作女神亲授制度的史实。
奥维德后来另写努马死后的埃革里亚：她退入阿里奇亚的林谷，不断哭泣，连希波吕托斯讲述自身苦难也不能使她停止悲伤。狄安娜最终怜悯她，把她化成清冷的泉水。于是国王留下祭祀制度，女神则以泉水延续哀悼；这是诗人的后续叙事，不应与李维的文字混作同一记录。

en.title: Numa and Egeria in the Sacred Grove
en.summary: Numa seeks to turn Rome from constant warfare toward regulated religious life. He attributes his instructions to meetings with Egeria beside a woodland spring. Later poetry follows the grieving goddess after his death, giving their association a different, watery ending.
paragraphs: After Romulus, Roman tradition made Numa the city’s second king. He sought to temper a population accustomed to warfare by establishing religious obligations and a shared calendar. Livy describes his solitary visits to a grove with a spring, where he claimed to meet the goddess Egeria. Instructions attributed to her gave divine authority to the practices he introduced among the Romans.

Numa organized priestly offices, assigned the care of particular rites, and regulated the calendar so that public worship followed an established order. Meetings in the grove provided a sacred explanation for these decisions, not a transcript that other citizens could examine. Livy also presents the claim as a ruler’s means of governing minds; it should not be mistaken for verified divine legislation.

Ovid later tells what happened to Egeria after Numa died. She withdrew to the wooded valley at Aricia and wept inconsolably; even Hippolytus’s account of his own suffering could not relieve her grief. Diana finally transformed the mourning nymph into a cool spring. The king left religious institutions behind, while this poetic continuation gave his companion an enduring form of lament.
